script: Caffeine blocks the signal that makes you feel tired. It does not add energy - it hides the debt. Green tea carries theanine alongside it, which is why tea tends to feel smoother than the same caffeine from coffee. General information, not medical advice. Talk to a doctor about what fits you.

script: Creatine is the most studied sports supplement there is. Your muscles store it as phosphocreatine, and use it to recycle energy during short, hard efforts. script: Magnesium is not one thing. What it is bound to changes how much you absorb. Most people get some from food. Seeds, greens, beans, whole grains. script: Melatonin is a timing signal, not a sedative. It tells your body it is night. Bright light late in the evening delays that signal. Which is why the phone is part of the problem. The clearest use in the research is jet lag and shifted schedules - moving the clock, not forcing sleep. For ordinary bad sleep, the dull advice still beats the bottle: same wake time, dark room, less light at night. General information, not medical advice. Talk to a doctor about what fits you.

script: Your skin makes vitamin D from sunlight. That is the whole reason this one is complicated. Far from the equator, in winter, the sun sits too low for your skin to make much of it at all. Some comes from food. Oily fish, egg yolks, fortified milk. It is one of the few where a blood test actually tells you where you stand, instead of guessing. General information, not medical advice. Talk to a doctor about what fits you.
